turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
Fixed. The LLM was actually returning those tasks; the app was throwing them away afterward.

**The cause:** in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:235`, after the summary came back, a regex dropped any action item that didn't contain a deadline word (by, due, next, tomorrow, a weekday and so on) or a digit. "Priya will send the contract" matches none of those, so it got deleted.

**What I changed:**
- **Removed that filter.** Now every action item the model returns is kept. If the field comes back missing or malformed, it falls back to an empty list.
- **Updated the default summary prompt** (line 202). It now asks for items as "Owner: task", and for anything with an owner but no date it adds "no date given" instead of skipping it. This matches the rules already in `electron/llm/prompts.ts`, which said to keep these items. The post-processing filter was the only thing contradicting them.

**Not verified:** I couldn't type-check or run it. There's no `node_modules` in this copy of the repo, and the sandbox blocked downloading TypeScript from npm. The change is small: one block removed and one prompt string edited. To confirm, run a short meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract" and check that it shows up in the recap.

One more thing: if you have a mode active, like Team Meet, the recap uses that mode's sections instead. That path never had this filter, so it wasn't affected.

My first fix only covered a path the app hardly ever uses. This should cover the path your recaps actually go through. I couldn't run it, though: there's no `node_modules` here and the sandbox blocks npm.

**Why the first fix didn't work:** the database creates a "General" mode on install and marks it active (`electron/db/DatabaseManager.ts:471`). When a mode is active, the recap prompt asks the model to fill that mode's note sections. It never uses the generic prompt I edited before. The mode prompt says "extract only what is present" and has no rule about tasks without a date, so the model kept leaving them out. Groq also has its own separate prompt, and its only example action item had a date ("by Wednesday").

**What I changed this time:**
- **Shared base rules** (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:144`): both the mode prompt and the generic prompt use these, so this is the change that matters. Action items must be written as "Owner: task". Anything with an owner but no date must still be included, ending with "(no date given)". The model must never invent a date.
- **Groq prompt** (`electron/llm/prompts.ts`): added the same rule, plus a second example: `"Priya: Send the contract (no date given)"`.
- **The deadline filter I removed last time** stays removed. Nothing after the model filters action items.

**One more possible cause:** if you use the Team Meet mode, its Action Items section is described as "All action items that were said **I** would do after the meeting." That leaves out Priya's tasks whether or not they have a date. Sales and Recruiting have the same "I" wording. These descriptions are stored per mode in the database, so you can edit the section description in that mode's settings. Or I can change the default wording to "all action items, with owner" and add a migration that updates modes still using the default text. Want me to?

To test: end a short meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract". The recap should show "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)". If it doesn't, tell me which mode was active and which provider you were on (Groq, custom, etc.).

I'm stopping the blind edits. I've now read every place that touches action items, and nothing in this source still drops tasks that have no deadline. The more likely problem is that the app you're testing isn't running this code.

**Why I think the app is running older code:**
- This checkout has no `node_modules`, no `dist`, and no `dist-electron`. It has never been built or installed, so the app you're testing can't be built from it.
- The Electron side is compiled before it runs (`npm run build:electron`, or `npm start`, which builds first). Until you rebuild in the folder you actually launch from, my edits aren't in it. If you're using an installed copy of the app, you need a new `npm run app:build`.

**What I checked after the last round:**
- **Saving and display:** `MeetingDetails.tsx` just renders whatever was saved. That covers the action items list and the mode sections. The PDF export and DB update don't filter anything either.
- **The LLM response handler:** `processResponse` in `LLMHelper.ts:566` only strips formatting. It rejects the whole response if it contains "I'm not sure" or "I don't know", but it never filters individual items.
- **The deadline regex** from the first round is gone, and no other filter like it exists in the repo.

**The one remaining cause in this code:** if your active mode is Team Meet, Sales or Recruiting, its Action Items section only asks for "action items that were said I would do." Priya's task is left out because it isn't yours, whether or not it has a date. You can fix that in the mode's section description in settings, or I can change the default wording and add a migration that updates existing modes.

To pin it down I need three things:
1. How do you launch the app: `npm start` from some folder, or an installed app?
2. Which mode was active when you ended the meeting?
3. What does "not working" look like now: is Priya's item missing entirely, or does it show up wrong?

If you can paste the `[MeetingPersistence] Raw LLM summary response` line from the console after ending a meeting, that will show whether the model is leaving the item out or the app is.
